questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Define road safety.
questions.a: Road safety is the practice of using roads in ways that prevent accidents and protect road users.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention six road users.
questions.a: Pedestrians, drivers, passengers, cyclists, motorcyclists and animal handlers.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention three types of traffic signs.
questions.a: Warning signs, regulatory signs and information signs.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five causes of road accidents.
questions.a: Over-speeding, drunk driving, reckless driving, careless crossing and using mobile phones while driving.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five effects of road accidents.
questions.a: Death, injuries, disability, damage to property and loss of income.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five road safety rules for pedestrians.
questions.a: Use footpaths, cross at safe places, obey traffic signals, avoid playing on roads and remain alert.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five road safety rules for drivers.
questions.a: Obey traffic rules, avoid over-speeding, wear seat belts, avoid drunk driving and maintain vehicles properly.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give four road safety rules for passengers.
questions.a: Wear seat belts, sit properly, do not distract the driver and keep body parts inside the vehicle.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give four safety rules for cyclists.
questions.a: Wear a helmet, obey traffic rules, maintain the bicycle and use lights or reflectors when necessary.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give four safety rules for motorcyclists.
questions.a: Wear a helmet, obey traffic rules, avoid speeding and maintain the motorcycle.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.a: It means stop.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What does a green traffic light mean?
questions.a: It means proceed when the way is clear and safe.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a zebra crossing?
questions.a: It is a marked place on a road where pedestrians can cross.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a helmet?
questions.a: A helmet is protective headgear worn to protect the head.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a seat belt?
questions.a: A seat belt is a safety device used to secure a person in a vehicle.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should children not play on roads?
questions.a: Because they may be hit by vehicles and seriously injured or killed.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should drivers not use mobile phones while driving?
questions.a: Because mobile phones distract drivers and reduce their concentration on the road.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should motorcyclists wear helmets?
questions.a: To protect their heads and reduce the severity of head injuries during crashes.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should passengers wear seat belts?
questions.a: Seat belts help protect passengers during sudden stops or collisions.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention five ways of preventing road accidents.
questions.a: Obey traffic rules, avoid speeding, avoid drunk driving, use safe crossing points and maintain vehicles properly.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the responsibility of every road user?
questions.a: Every road user should use the road responsibly, obey traffic rules and protect the safety of other road users.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Define a debate.
questions.a: A debate is a formal discussion in which people give arguments for or against a motion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a motion?
questions.a: A motion is a statement or proposal presented for discussion in a debate.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a proposer?
questions.a: A proposer is a person who supports the motion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is an opposer?
questions.a: An opposer is a person who argues against the motion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five roles of a chairperson.
questions.a: The chairperson introduces the motion, controls the debate, gives speakers turns, maintains order and ensures that rules are followed.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four responsibilities of a secretary.
questions.a: The secretary takes notes, records important points, records information about the debate and keeps the debate records.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of a timekeeper?
questions.a: A timekeeper keeps track of the time given to speakers.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention five debate vocabulary words.
questions.a: Motion, proposer, opposer, argument and chairperson.
accepted: Motion, proposer, opposer, argument and chairperson.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a point of order?
questions.a: It is a formal interruption concerning the rules or procedure of the debate.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a point of information?
questions.a: It is a brief question or piece of information directed to a speaker according to the rules of the debate.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a point of inquiry?
questions.a: It is a question raised to seek clarification or information.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five qualities of a good debater.
questions.a: A good debater should be confident, well prepared, respectful, clear in speech and a good listener.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five rules of debating.
questions.a: Speakers should listen to others, respect other views, avoid insults, speak clearly and keep within the given time.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should learners research debate topics?
questions.a: Research helps learners obtain information and prepare strong arguments.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should learners make notes during a debate?
questions.a: Notes help learners remember important arguments and respond appropriately.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is direct speech?
questions.a: Direct speech gives the exact words spoken by a person.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is indirect speech?
questions.a: Indirect speech reports what someone said without giving the exact words.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write one sentence using "even though".
questions.a: Even though the speaker disagreed with me, I respected her opinion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write one sentence using "although".
questions.a: Although the argument was interesting, it was not supported by facts.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write one sentence using "if".
questions.a: If I were the chairperson, I would give both sides equal opportunities to speak.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write one sentence using "whereas".
questions.a: The proposer supports the motion, whereas the opposer rejects it.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should speakers respond appropriately to arguments?
questions.a: They should respond appropriately so that the debate remains respectful, relevant and meaningful.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why is debating important to learners?
questions.a: Debating develops communication, confidence, critical thinking, research, reasoning and leadership skills.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a family?
questions.a: A family is a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption who live together or care for one another.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four types of families.
questions.a: Nuclear family, extended family, single-parent family and child-headed family.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a nuclear family?
questions.a: A nuclear family consists of a father, mother and their children.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is an extended family?
questions.a: An extended family consists of parents, children and other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, aunts, nephews, nieces and cousins.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a cousin?
questions.a: A cousin is a child of one's uncle or aunt.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is an uncle?
questions.a: An uncle is the brother of one's father or mother.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five importance of a family.
questions.a: Any five: it provides love and care; food and shelter; education and guidance; protection from danger; it teaches good behaviour; it gives emotional support; it helps members in difficult times; it promotes unity and cooperation; it teaches cultural values.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five ways of promoting good family relationships.
questions.a: Any five: respecting one another; loving one another; sharing responsibilities; helping one another; communicating openly; forgiving one another; solving disagreements peacefully; caring for the elderly; spending time together; being honest.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four causes of poor family relationships.
questions.a: Any four: lack of communication; poverty; domestic violence; alcohol and drug abuse; disrespect; neglect; dishonesty; quarrels; separation of parents.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State four effects of poor family relationships.
questions.a: Any four: family conflicts; stress and unhappiness; poor academic performance; child neglect; domestic violence; separation of family members; loss of trust; school dropout.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is an occupation?
questions.a: An occupation is the work that a person does regularly to earn a living or provide a service.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five examples of occupations.
questions.a: Any five: farming, teaching, fishing, trading, carpentry, nursing, driving, building, tailoring, banking.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is farming?
questions.a: Farming is the growing of crops and keeping of animals for food, raw materials and income.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four types of farmers.
questions.a: Any four: crop farmers, poultry farmers, dairy farmers, fish farmers, pig farmers.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State four importance of farming.
questions.a: Any four: it provides food; provides employment; provides raw materials for industries; provides income; provides goods for export; supports other businesses.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is trading?
questions.a: Trading is the buying and selling of goods and services.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention three examples of traders.
questions.a: Any three: shopkeepers, wholesalers, retailers, market vendors.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a teacher?
questions.a: A teacher is a person who teaches — one who helps people acquire knowledge, skills and good behaviour.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a carpenter?
questions.a: A carpenter is a person who does carpentry — making and repairing things mainly from wood.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four products made by carpenters.
questions.a: Any four: chairs, tables, beds, doors, cupboards.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: State five factors considered when choosing an occupation.
questions.a: Any five: ability and talent; level of education; personal interests; skills; availability of employment; income expected; working conditions; availability of training; demand for the occupation; health and physical ability.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give five importance of occupations.
questions.a: Any five: they provide income; provide employment; provide goods and services; improve standards of living; promote economic development; generate government revenue; promote self-reliance; develop people's skills.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is fishing?
questions.a: Fishing is the catching or rearing of fish for food and income.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention three occupations related to transport.
questions.a: Any three: driver, pilot, sailor, mechanic, motorcycle rider.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why are occupations important to a country?
questions.a: Because they provide income and employment, provide goods and services, promote economic development, generate government revenue and contribute to national development.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a hotel?
questions.a: A hotel is a building or establishment where people pay to stay, eat and receive other services while away from home.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a hotel guest?
questions.a: A hotel guest is a person who stays in a hotel.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why do people stay in hotels?
questions.a: People stay in hotels to get accommodation, food, drinks and other services when they are away from home.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention five services offered by hotels.
questions.a: Any five: accommodation, food and drinks, laundry services, room cleaning, internet services.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is accommodation?
questions.a: Accommodation is a place where people stay or live temporarily.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a hotel manager?
questions.a: A hotel manager is a person who supervises the activities of a hotel.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Who is a receptionist?
questions.a: A receptionist is a hotel worker who welcomes guests, records their details and helps them with accommodation.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of a chef?
questions.a: A chef prepares food for hotel guests.
accepted: A chef prepares food for hotel guests.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of a waiter or waitress?
questions.a: A waiter or waitress serves food and drinks to guests.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of a housekeeper?
questions.a: A housekeeper keeps hotel rooms and other areas clean and tidy.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of a security guard in a hotel?
questions.a: A security guard protects the hotel, workers and guests from danger.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of a gardener in a hotel?
questions.a: A gardener maintains flowers, lawns, trees and other plants around the hotel.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention five people who work in a hotel.
questions.a: Any five: hotel manager, receptionist, chef, waiter or waitress, housekeeper, security guard, gardener.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention four types of hotels.
questions.a: Budget hotels, luxury hotels, resort hotels and business hotels.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why are hotels important?
questions.a: Because they provide accommodation, food and other services to travellers.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How do hotels provide employment?
questions.a: Hotels employ people such as managers, receptionists, chefs, waiters, housekeepers and security guards.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How do hotels promote tourism?
questions.a: Hotels provide accommodation and other services to tourists, making it easier for them to visit and stay in different places.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How do hotels contribute to the development of a country?
questions.a: Hotels create employment, generate income, pay taxes and support other businesses.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention five rules that hotel guests should follow.
questions.a: Keep hotel rooms clean; respect hotel workers and other guests; avoid damaging hotel property; pay for services received; follow hotel rules.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What can happen if hotel guests damage hotel property?
questions.a: They may be required to pay for the damaged property and may face other action according to hotel rules.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a dictionary?
questions.a: A dictionary is a reference book that gives information about words, including their meanings, spellings and pronunciations.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Mention five uses of a dictionary.
questions.a: A dictionary is used to find meanings, check spelling, check pronunciation, learn new words and understand how words are used.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What are guide words?
questions.a: Guide words are words printed at the top of dictionary pages that help users locate words quickly.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a thesaurus?
questions.a: A thesaurus is a reference book used mainly to find words with similar or related meanings and opposites.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is an abbreviation?
questions.a: An abbreviation is a shortened form of a word or group of words.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is an acronym?
questions.a: An acronym is a word formed from the initial letters of other words.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is alphabetical order?
questions.a: Alphabetical order is the arrangement of words according to the order of letters in the alphabet.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Why should we learn to use a dictionary?
questions.a: We should learn to use a dictionary so that we can find information about words independently and improve our English.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What should you do whenever you find a difficult word?
questions.a: Whenever I find a difficult word, I should refer to the dictionary to find its meaning and other information about it.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How does a dictionary help us to pronounce words correctly?
questions.a: It provides pronunciation information that shows how words should be spoken.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How does a dictionary help us to spell words correctly?
questions.a: It provides the standard spelling of words, allowing us to check and correct our spelling.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How does dictionary work help us become independent learners?
questions.a: It teaches us how to find information about unfamiliar words without always depending on another person.
